title: Update from the Exit Theory project
body:
Hey everybody! I just wanted to write to the community with an update on my book project *Exit Theory*, for which I received a generous grant of EDG a few months ago.

We went a little out-of-order (doing some things for Milestone 2 now, postponing some things in Milestone 1), but altogether I think we’ve delivered more than enough for a first milestone—so I just wanted to take a moment to check in.

- We published [a landing page](https://jmrphy.ck.page/a16bb26647) for the project, mentioning Edgeware and the grant.
- We [published a video](https://youtu.be/6E3LMFzIHXc) mentioning Edgeware, the grant, and showing off some behind-the-scenes shots of the Edgeware interfaces. The Edgeware spot starts around [8:45.](https://youtu.be/6E3LMFzIHXc?t=525)
- I featured Edgeware in [ȘȈǤƝȘ 63: Reality Splitters](https://www.otherlife.co/signs-reality-splitters/#other-life-edgeware-agency), with a link to the Edgeware Discord.
- I featured Edgeware [on the podcast](https://podcast.otherlife.co/episodes/63-reality-splitters-based-mansion-2), with a link to the Edgeware Discord.
- We onboarded some Edgeware community members who claimed their free memberships in IndieThinkers.org. Jake Naviasky actually published one of the most extensively discussed posts in all of 2021.
- And most importantly, I’ve made progress on the book. Not quite enough to show off yet, but I am writing, and making it a public commitment has been great to lock in the focus and momentum.

I think we under-delivered on our planned contributions to the DAO working group. This fell through the cracks for a few different reasons, but I take full responsibility for it. I will more than make up for it, see below.

## Next steps

I’ve decided that I don’t think I’d like to take any more money from the Edgeware community.
